180	
181	Every interactive component must define normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focused, success, warning, and error states where relevant. Status must combine color with an icon and plain-language label.
182	
183	## Accessibility
184	
185	- Normal text requires at least 4.5:1 contrast; 3:1 is allowed only for large text.
186	- Essential control boundaries and state indicators require 3:1.
187	- Keyboard focus uses a visible 2 DIP ring and may not rely on a fill-color change alone.
188	- Orbit on White measures 12.07:1 in the source design system.
189	- Bloom on Ink measures 6.62:1.
190	- Light secondary text measures 6.89:1 on White.
191	- Dark secondary text measures 10.95:1 on Ink.
192	
193	## Writing UI code
194	
195	Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
196	exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from the design system and
197	from the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
198	only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.
199	
200	1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
201	   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
202	   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
203	   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
204	   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
205	   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
206	   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
207	   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
208	   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
209	2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
210	   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
211	   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
212	   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
213	   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
214	   value that exists in the design artifacts but not in the roles or scales is a design
215	   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
216	3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
217	   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
218	   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
219	4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
220	   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
221	   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
222	5. **The design system wins when it and the code disagree.** The two Claude
223	   artifacts are the source of truth (Kenneth, 2026-10-20; Figma is
224	   retired): the Design System
225	   (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the "JusPrin v2"
226	   canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). The canvas
227	   frozen on 2026-10-27 (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v)
228	   is history, not a source. Change the token file to match, or, when the
229	   code's value is the one to keep, change the artifact first. Do not trust
230	   old commit messages about either.
231	6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
232	   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
233	   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
234	   not that the result looks right.
235	7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
236	   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
237	   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
238	   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.
239	
240	## Runtime application in the native app
241	
242	The token file is applied to the running application in three layers. All
243	three read `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`; none of them carries a
244	color literal of its own, and the whole layer touches OrcaSlicer code in only
245	three small, additive seams plus one attachment point.
246	
247	1. **Fork-owned surfaces** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/*`, the React Agent
248	   page) resolve every style through the token file, not only color.
249	   - Native: `ShellTheme` exposes `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for
250	     the radius and spacing scales and the per-component sizes, `font(role)`
251	     for the type roles above. It is loaded once, by `Brand/BrandPalette.cpp`, and passed
252	     by reference into every shell widget. Widgets that paint themselves read
253	     it directly; a stock `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button`
254	     is dressed through the three functions in `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, so no
255	     fork-owned C++ file names an OrcaSlicer font preset or writes a radius as
256	     a number. `tests/jusprin/test_shell_theme.cpp` checks the parse and the
257	     fonts.
258	   - Web: `AgentUI/src/tokens.ts` writes the semantic colors as
259	     `--<group>-<name>` on every appearance change, and once at startup the
260	     radii as `--radius-<name>` and each type role as a complete `font`
261	     shorthand, `--font-<role>` in the UI face, plus `--font-code` for the one
262	     monospace role. The stylesheet may only say `var(--…)` for color, radius,
263	     and type; `AgentUI/src/styles.test.ts` reads the stylesheet from disk and
264	     fails on any literal, and on any spacing value off the scale.
265	   - Canvas: the Prepare canvas's tool strip (`Canvas/ViewportToolStrip`)
266	     paints with ImGui inside the GL frame, from the same `ShellTheme`. Its
267	     icons are the `currentColor` SVGs in `resources/jusprin/ui/icons`,
268	     rasterized white and tinted with the token colour. ImGui 1.83 has no
269	     shadow primitive, so `elevation.medium` is approximated with stacked
270	     translucent rounded rectangles.
271	2. **Retained OrcaSlicer surfaces** are retinted through the color tables
272	   OrcaSlicer already routes its colors through, installed once per appearance
273	   mode by `JusPrin/Brand/BrandPalette.cpp` from the end of
274	   `GUI_App::init_label_colours`:
275	   - `StateColor::SetColorOverrides` maps OrcaSlicer's brand and surface
276	     literals (teal family, grays, whites, text grays) to semantic tokens before
277	     OrcaSlicer's own dark-mode remap runs. Every widget built on `StateColor`
278	     switches at once.
279	   - `BitmapCache::SetColorReplaces` rewrites the teal in the SVG icon set to
280	     the action color at load time, and the monochrome brand mark to the text
281	     color.
282	   - `ColorRGB::orca_accent()` replaces OrcaSlicer's own accent, the teal
283	     behind `ColorRGB::ORCA()`, `ColorRGBA::ORCA()`, `ImGuiWrapper::COL_ORCA`
284	     and the preview sliders' `BRAND_COLOR`, with the action color. That
285	     recolours the ImGui and GL layer: the preview sliders' handles, filled
286	     track and value text, gizmo highlights, the selection rectangle. Every
287	     reader evaluates it at use; ImGui's style table, filled once at start-up,
288	     is filled again through `ImGuiWrapper::reset_style`. The sliders' greys,
289	     value boxes and handle shape, the legend and the bed stay OrcaSlicer's.
290	   - The canvas selection is OrcaSlicer's own, unretinted: its silhouette
291	     outline, which OrcaSlicer ships switched off and the shell switches on
292	     while it is installed, plus its white corner brackets. The brackets were
293	     briefly given the primary action color; on the dark build plate that
294	     measured 1.29:1 in light mode against white's 9:1, and with the outline
295	     carrying the selection the override was dropped on 2026-09-21, which
296	     left `Selection` untouched by the fork again.
297	   - The ImGui panels, the canvas selection rectangle, and the About dialog
298	     are left alone in source: those surfaces are slated to be hidden or
299	     replaced, so editing them would be divergence with no lasting value.
300	   - The mapping table in `BrandPalette.cpp` is the reviewed teal-to-purple
301	     decision. Extend it there; never add a purple literal to an OrcaSlicer file.
302	   - Widgets that paint the teal without going through `StateColor` (hyperlinks,
303	     the settings tab underline, notification accents, Bambu-only dialogs) are
304	     deliberately left teal; the cost of editing them in busy upstream files
305	     outweighs surfaces JusPrin rarely or never shows.
306	3. **Identity** comes from two data-only mechanisms:
307	   - `resources/jusprin/overlay/images/` holds the splash, About and horizontal
308	     lockups, monochrome mark, wizard watermark, and window icons under
309	     OrcaSlicer's own asset names. `Slic3r::var()` checks that directory
310	     first, so no logo call site is edited. See the README there.
311	   - `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` builds `resources/i18n/<lang>/<app key>.mo`
312	     from upstream's `.po` files with the product name substituted, plus an
313	     English catalog for the source strings, so every language reads "JusPrin"
314	     without touching a string or macro in upstream code. Attribution strings
315	     in About are excluded by the script.
316	   - The generic printer profiles' plate texture,
317	     `resources/profiles/Custom/orcaslicer_bed_texture.svg`, is overwritten
318	     with the JusPrin lockup; the file name stays because five profiles
319	     reference it.
320	
321	`tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` fails the build if a token edit breaks the
322	contrast rules above or leaves a token in one mode without its counterpart in
323	the other. The same test guards the radius, spacing, and type scales: the
324	`dimension.radius`, `dimension.space`, and `typography.roles` tables must match
325	the values in this document exactly, `typography.code` must stay a single
326	12/16 role, every component radius must be one of the scale values, and every
327	button recipe must name a type role rather than a raw size.
328	
329	Known gaps, all deliberate: ImGui panels and canvas notifications keep the
330	teal accent; the first-run setup wizard (an OrcaSlicer HTML page) is
331	Orca-branded until JusPrin's own onboarding replaces it; the About dialog
332	links to the OrcaSlicer website; vendor printer profiles other than the
333	generic ones keep their own plate textures; dark mode and the Preview canvas
334	were not visually verified.
335	
336	## Design handoff requirements
337	
338	Every high-fidelity product frame must:
339	
340	1. Define each application screen in one canonical appearance mode. Do not
341	   create paired light and dark screen frames. The other mode must be
342	   deterministically derived by the design system from the same semantic token
343	   names, component variants, geometry, content, and interaction state. Verify
344	   light/dark differences in the design-system primitives and semantic mappings
345	   rather than duplicating every application screen.
346	2. State the mode, viewport, component variants, keyboard focus, and any deliberate exception.
347	3. Use DIP, native density, and the design system's radius scale.
348	4. Use HarmonyOS Sans SC for product UI, and monospace only for code (the design system's `code` style uses the system monospace font).
349	5. Show normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focus, error, warning, and success states as applicable.
350	6. Test long filenames, localized labels, dense settings, empty states, and narrow windows.
351	7. Use the logo files in `resources/jusprin/branding/` and the existing functional icon system.
352	8. Label and justify any value that is not in the token files.
353	9. Draw a repeated feature composition, such as the setup card, chat header, composer or printer-and-spool chip, once, on the Compositions page of the JusPrin v2 canvas, and import it into screens by name. Never paste a copy into a screen.
354	10. Change the boards before the code (Kenneth, 2026-11-07). Once a UI change is decided, edit the boards on the JusPrin v2 canvas, publish them, and tell Kenneth which boards changed and what they show; start the code only after that. If the code turns up something the boards did not foresee, update the boards before writing the code that follows from it. A fix that changes nothing on screen needs no board.
355	11. Update an existing board when the change fits it; when it needs a new board, mark the old ones (Kenneth, 2026-11-08). Before publishing a new board, look on every page of the canvas for older boards of the same screen or state, not only the ones beside it. Put a note beside each one, on its own page: "Superseded <date> by <the new boards>. Kept as a record." When no newer board draws that screen, the note says "Outdated" instead and names what no longer matches. Name the boards you marked when you report the change. From 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-08, three of the four batches of replacement boards left older boards on other pages unmarked.
356	
357	The POC decks, rendered examples, horizontal lockup PNG, and generation sources remain available for visual-reference work through [POC reference](poc-reference.md). They are not runtime dependencies.

Added then: `surface-raised-hover` (menu-row highlight, dark #3B3047) and `component-composer-maxLines` (8); the new Composer is drawn by `tools/composer/composer_html.py`. Publishing (2026-10-20, filament step): a publish is refused as "haven't viewed the latest version" unless this session did a plain `read` of the artifact url (path reads alone do not count). Headless Chrome hangs when another Chrome holds the default profile: pass `--user-data-dir=` (render.py now does). MenuRow has `detail`, `detailTone: 'warning'` and `meta` since then. **Trap found 2026-10-20 (turn line work):** `figma-mirror/tools/bundle.src.js`, `bundle.src.css` and `index.src.d.ts` were STALE against the live Design System bundle (menu-row detail/meta and the Composer menus had been added directly in the artifact). Patch the live files (published/… copies, verified equal to the artifact by sha) and refresh the tools sources from the patched result; `tools/composer/add_turn_line_boards.py` and the ChatTurnActivity card were done that way. The DS page generates `tokens.css` itself: never publish it to the DS, only to the canvas's `project/ds/jusprin/` copy. Adding a coded component = patch bundle.js (function + header list + __EXPORTS__), bundle.css, index.d.ts (props + window typing), tokens.json, a hand-written `components//preview.html` card with `@dsCard height=` measured by rendering it with React from unpkg, README.md's component list, and `design-system.json` lastChange in the last call. **2026-10-26 (setup card rework):** `tools/composer/setup_card_lib.py` draws the two-part card as board markup, spec lines and the coded component from one props dict; `build_setup_card_rework.py` runs the whole rework (cards, screens, calibration, sticky, new, canvas, ds) into `work-setup-card/`. The mirror's `published/canvas` had drifted by three onboarding-v1 boards (fetched back); the live canvas.json, not the mirror's, is the base for an index publish. Version ids before and after each publish are logged in the README ("Versions before the setup-card rework"): the tool cannot list versions, so write them down at publish time. Both artifacts' versions bump when their Artifact type re-releases, so a new version id alone does not mean content changed. `tools/bundle.src.*` and `index.src.d.ts` were refreshed from the published bundle; `heights.json` in the work dir holds every measured board height. --- name: canvas-boards-from-bundle-rules description: "Kenneth's 2026-10-21 correction: a canvas board I draw must copy the Design System bundle's CSS rules and the app's own markup, never an older board or memory; the calibration page had 14 px menu rows drawn at 13, a missing Connect… row, a black Remove, a stale reply-choice style and more." metadata: node_type: memory type: feedback originSessionId: 9ce2f3c8-7b6d-4ba7-99ce-889f9d9f192a modified: 2026-10-22T00:09:35.890Z --- Kenneth, 2026-10-21, on the calibration page I drew: "It looks like you didn't follow this hygiene. read design guidelines in readme, and fix your own sloppiness", then "I suspect there were more sloppiness in the boards you designed". He was right on both counts. I had copied markup from older canvas boards (the printer-menu board at 13 px rows, the stale ds-chat-reply-choice board) and from memory (a Home kebab with no Connect…, a black Remove, a 220 px width, the filament menu in an old order), instead of from the two sources that are authoritative. **Why:** rule 5 of "Writing UI code" (agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md) says the design system wins, and the design system's truth is its coded bundle (`figma-mirror/published/ds/project/components/bundle.css`, classes `.jp-*`), not any one board on the canvas: boards drift (the printer-menu board draws rows at 13 px, the reply choice board draws the pre-capsule style). For surfaces the bundle has no component for (the printer receipt, a sent photo in a message), the app's own CSS and TSX are the source. **How to apply:** before drawing a board, dump the bundle rules for every component used (`grep '\.jp-' bundle.css`) and read the app's row set for every menu (Shell/PrinterMenu.cpp, Shell/FilamentMenu.cpp, HomeUI PrinterMenu.tsx) and the app's CSS for chat pieces (AgentUI/styles.css). Draw rows at Body 14 / 36 px (`.jp-menu-row`), popovers on surface-raised 280 wide, reply choices as capsules on surface-subtle, user bubbles 10/12 padding radius-medium at 75% width, tool cards on surface-subtle, project cards 293 wide with one status line, and no annotation tags ("NEW") inside a drawn component. Needs a work dir holding the live files and runtime/." metadata: node_type: memory type: reference originSessionId: 3eabf4a3-87b6-4471-a4e5-b6fb9c14763a modified: 2026-11-02T03:18:24.462Z --- `python3 figma-mirror/tools/composer/render_dc.py [--dark] ...` serves `/project`, maps `support.js` to `/runtime/dc-runtime.js` (the artifact's `artifact-type/dc-runtime.js`) and `/_blob/` through `/runtime/blobs.json`, and shoots headless Chrome at 2x with its own `--user-data-dir`. 21 boards take about 22 s. `--dark` flips the board's theme prop. If you have to draw a new board, make sure you mark the old ones superseded." **Why:** between 2026-11-01 and 11-08 every batch of replacement boards marked the older boards next to it but missed others. The first-run batch (11-03) marked the wizard but not credits-01b. The money batch (11-06) marked credits-05a/b but not credits-04a/b/c on the Agent setup page, and credits-07a/7b still say "Pay as you go" with the alert switch on Account. Related: [[update-design-before-code]], [[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]. --- name: show-design-in-the-screen description: "Kenneth, 2026-10-28: a design board for review must show the change inside the whole screen it lives in (real viewport, the pane, the header), never a component drawn alone; he rejected header-strip-only boards as drawn 'out of thin air in the vacuum'." metadata: node_type: memory type: feedback originSessionId: 4219b55f-d6b6-4807-b23b-1c973a54c315 modified: 2026-10-28T15:41:05.547Z --- On 2026-10-28 I published four boards for the "from the file" printer-chip mark: the header strip alone, the chip's states, the menu popover, the header after a choice. Kenneth: "So you drew the mark out of the thin air in the vacuum? Where should they be attached to? … do you know how to show a design to a human being?" He was looking at the Printer & Material Settings page, where every board is a whole 1280×800 Prepare screen. **Why:** a reviewer judges a change by what surrounds it: the bed it sits over, the pane beside it, the message that follows. A strip with no screen gives nothing to attach the change to. **How to apply:** every review board is the whole screen at the app's size (1280×800 for Prepare), composed the way the canvas's existing screens are: header, viewport, Agent pane with the shared components (`comp-chat-header`, `comp-pinned-setup-card`, `comp-composer` via ``), and the timeline rows the app really showed. Use the walkthrough's real screenshots for the viewport (crop, upload as a canvas asset, ``), and the app's real strings. A component-states board may come last, as a detail, never first or alone. Related: [[canvas-boards-from-bundle-rules]], [[file-printer-switch-decisions]]. --- name: update-design-before-code description: For any JusPrin UI change, update the canvas boards first and show Kenneth, then write the code; never code first and redraw the boards afterwards metadata: type: feedback --- Kenneth, 2026-11-07: "I want you to update the design first before doing the coding." He said it right after the in-app sign-in change ([[sign-in-is-the-in-app-form-everywhere]]). That time the code (shared SignInDoor, the Preferences bridge messages, tests) was written first, and the canvas boards were redrawn only afterwards, in versions 140 and 141. **Why:** the canvas is the design source of truth ([[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]). When the code comes first, the boards end up copying whatever the code happened to do. Kenneth then has no chance to change the design before code exists. **How to apply:** once a UI change is decided, edit the boards on the current canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ) first, publish them, and tell Kenneth which boards changed and what they show. Start the code only after that. If the code turns up something the boards didn't foresee, update the boards before writing the code that follows from it. Small fixes that change nothing on screen don't need a board. --- name: mockup-strings-from-real-output description: "UI sketches that summarise data must use strings a rule produced from real data, never hand-typed ideal text" metadata: node_type: memory type: feedback originSessionId: 9cbf10d8-8485-416c-81ef-f11d3e2c8b83 modified: 2026-10-08T12:57:29.751Z --- When sketching UI that summarises OrcaSlicer data (the setup summary card, 2026-10-07/08), do not hand-type ideal strings such as "Brim 8 mm outer" or a shortened preset name. Kenneth challenged exactly those: there was no rule that produces them, and measuring showed they did not fit the line either. **Why:** Kenneth said an earlier agent drew a good-looking mockup, then at implementation found no way from raw data to the "smart" summary and fell back to hard-coding a few fields (the 13-key `kSetupKeys` list). He wants that trap avoided, not repeated. **How to apply:** Before proposing a layout, write the generic rule, run it over real data (all settings, all shipped preset names), measure lengths against the real line width, and fill the sketch only from that output. Say plainly which phrasing only a model could write. He asked for a 5% random sample of the output to review, not the full table. The formatter is `Workspace/SettingDisplay.hpp`, tested by `setting_display_tests` (links libslic3r only, builds in minutes in a fresh worktree). See [[figma-dump-then-measure-parity]]. **2026-10-08 follow-up (finishing the Codex implementation, worktree `~/.codex/worktrees/setup-card-differences/JusPrin`, branch `codex/setup-card-differences`, uncommitted):** Kenneth said the other agent matched the design terribly. Its fixtures did match; what was wrong only showed in the real app and in what it deleted. Checks that found the defects, in the order worth repeating: - Restore the tests an agent deleted for behaviour the handoff said stays unchanged, then run them: this caught a saved card showing "Agent is applying…". - Pixel-diff, not eyeball: render the built fixtures into the mockup's own frame (same scaffold CSS, 320 px, light and dark), screenshot both with headless Chrome, `PIL.ImageChops.difference(...).getbbox()`. - Real app: `JusPrinShellHarness --light-ui|--dark-ui --setup-differences-capture ` edits process, filament, printer and object settings and photographs the web view. Use `capture_web_view` (WebKit snapshot); `write_screen_capture` gives blank 810-byte PNGs from a shell. - `Search::OptionsSearcher::get_option` only knows settings visible in the current user mode and returns a neighbour otherwise; `get_group_and_category(";")` (try `key#0` for per-extruder keys) is mode-independent. - `PREVIEW_OUT=... npx vitest run` with no filter lets every `*.preview.test.tsx` overwrite the same file; name the test. - Kenneth, same day: hard-coded setting names are "a big problem" wherever they are, not only on the card. The chat timeline's agent pill (`ChangeRows.tsx`) looked up "Wall loops" and infill by label; he wanted it shown with a screenshot and gone. Do not leave such code with a note; fix it and show before/after. - A live capture only proves the design if the app is in the mockup's state. Mine first showed a project with no recorded purpose, so the title and lines differed and he called it out. The harness mode now records a purpose and applies a patch through `host.tools().propose("intent_update" / "settings_apply_patch", …, )`, slices, and waits out the 60 s "Updated" window. - Landed 2026-10-08: cherry-picked onto `jusprin-newui` in the main checkout as 198c64606f (not pushed by me), after Kenneth rewrote the approval-removal history (eb45279cd5). `origin/temp/setup-card-differences` (4650dd3093) is the pre-rewrite copy. --- name: artifact-watch-crosstalk description: "Publishing a design artifact arms a comment watch with auto-replies in that session; when several sessions work on the same artifact, each one answers the others' comments. Stop the watch after publishing unless Kenneth wants that session to handle comments." metadata: node_type: memory type: feedback originSessionId: 184d4aaf-cfcf-432d-ac3c-191a0b1f6a05 modified: 2026-10-21T12:37:33.441Z --- On 2026-10-21 Kenneth found another session's canvas comments (a "Calibration · Printer & Filament" page) being auto-replied to and reported in this session, and asked how to make this session ignore it. Cause: every publish to a Claude artifact arms a watch with comment auto-replies in the publishing session. Two sessions working on the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v) or the Design System (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) both get every comment sent to Claude, wherever it is on the artifact. **Why:** the wrong session answers a thread about work it doesn't know, and its reply can contradict the session that owns the boards. **How to apply:** after a publish, stop the watch (ArtifactComments action "watch", on: false) unless Kenneth said this session owns the artifact's comments. Re-read the live artifact before publishing again, since another session may have published since. Related: [[jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact]], [[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]].

To compare Windows screenshots against macOS, run the same
`shell_integration_harness` fixture on both and capture each popup by window id.

**Why:** `screencapture` and any ScreenCaptureKit path fail from the Bash tool
("could not create image from display") — the Screen Recording grant belongs to a
process I cannot reach. The computer-use `app_screenshot` tool is the only route,
and it accepts a **raw CGWindowID**, not just ids from `app_list_windows`. Popups
never appear in `app_list_windows`, so enumerate them yourself.

**How to apply:**
- Build a tiny Swift lister (`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionOnScreenOnly)`
  filtered by pid). The fork's `HeaderMenu` popups show up at `layer=101`; the main
  window is `layer=0`. Feed that id to `app_screenshot` for native-resolution pixels.
- Drive clicks with a Swift `CGEvent` helper at **global** coords
  (window origin + local). The app need not be frontmost.
- Only the **chip halves** respond to synthetic clicks. The header's overflow "…",
  the split-button chevron, and the Home back button do not — that is a limitation
  of the automation, **not** an application bug. Use the harness's own
  `--header-visual` / `--review-visual` modes for those screens instead.

# Resource overlay

Files here replace the OrcaSlicer resource of the same name at runtime.
`Slic3r::var()` checks `overlay/images/` before `resources/images/`, so an
upstream call such as `ScalableBitmap(this, "OrcaSlicer_about", 125)` renders
the JusPrin artwork without any edit to the calling code. Keep the OrcaSlicer
file names; they are the lookup keys. An SVG here shadows an upstream PNG of
the same stem because the bitmap loaders try SVG first.

Current overlays: splash, About lockup, horizontal lockup, monochrome mark
(message dialogs), colour mark (`OrcaSlicer.svg`: message, release-note and
update dialogs), setup-wizard watermark, the window icon PNGs, and the Mac
Dock icon. All are generated by `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Brand/brand_logo.py`.

content.text:
The splash and About window are drawn on the canvas and ready for your review: https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ, on a new page called "Splash & About". I haven't written any app code yet. This session's branch was moved onto `ui-walkthrough`, because the worktree had been cut from an old `main` that's missing the OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 merge. It has no commits.

**What the boards show**
- **Splash (boards 01–03):** a 480×480 window opens where the main window last stood. It shows the stacked cone-and-name logo, "Version 2.0.0" in small grey text, and a thin 160-wide bar. A short purple segment slides back and forth along the bar every 1.2 s until the main window opens. It shows no loading-step text and no percentage. Board 02 shows the bar's motion frame by frame. Board 03 is the same splash with no bar.
- **About window (boards 04–05):** it opens over Home with a title row and a close button. Then come:
  - the horizontal logo
  - "Version 2.0.0", with "Built on OrcaSlicer 2.5.0" and "Build 374c5f72a1" under it
  - a "Copy version" button, which copies "JusPrin 2.0.0 (OrcaSlicer 2.5.0, build 374c5f72a1)" and reads "Copied" for 2 s
  - a "Get help" list with the email address, Discord and GitHub as links
  - a line saying JusPrin is free software under the AGPL v3, beside a "License…" button that opens OrcaSlicer's existing licences-and-credits window

  Board 05 shows the hover, Copied, keyboard-focus and link-hover states. No older boards drew a splash or an About window, so nothing needed a superseded note.

**One thing the agreed design didn't foresee**
The app's logs show the splash is up for about 10 s. For all of it the main thread is busy: about 5 s loading the built-in printer profiles, then about 5 s building the main window. Normal drawing stops while the main thread is busy, so a bar animated by a timer would sit still.

I tested this with a throwaway Mac app that blocked its main thread for 3 s. A bar animated by macOS Core Animation kept sliding the whole time, captured in frames 0.8 s apart. The macOS system spinner did not visibly turn. So on the Mac the bar really moves, with no extra line in OrcaSlicer's code.

Windows and Linux have no equivalent. A bar there would freeze as soon as the app gets busy, which looks like a hang. That's why board 03 exists.

**Decision needed: should the splash on Windows and Linux leave out the moving bar?**
This is your call because it changes the "moving indicator" you agreed to on two of the three platforms.
- **Leave out the bar on Windows and Linux (my pick):** they show board 03, the logo and version alone. It costs nothing more and nothing on screen looks frozen.
- **Draw the Windows splash from its own background thread:** the bar moves on Windows too. It's roughly 150 lines of Windows-only code that I can only check on the Windows test VM, and Linux would still have no bar.
- **Keep a bar that moves only between busy stretches:** this doesn't need extra upstream lines, but the bar would freeze for seconds and then jump.

Do you approve the boards as drawn, or want changes? I'll start the code once you've reviewed them and answered the Windows and Linux question.

2026-10-24 (import-behavior work, PR TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#38): adding EmptyPlateHint.cpp to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake` after committing made the next build re-run CMake. The configure step reads the git hash into `-DGIT_COMMIT_HASH=\"<sha>\"`, which is on every TU's command line, so the whole tree (libslic3r included) recompiled at -j4: roughly an hour.

Not the only cause of that symptom: if the build log starts with "premature end of file; recovering", see [[ninja-deps-bad-record-repeat-rebuild]].

2026-11-02 (connection-skill worktree): adding two new `AgentUI/src/skills/*/SKILL.md` files did the same. The jusprin_web target globs that tree, so the build printed "GLOB mismatch!", re-ran CMake and started 945 steps for jusprin_web + agent_bridge_tests + shell_integration_harness.

**Why:** a command-line change invalidates every object in ninja's log, not just the touched target.
**How to apply:** add new source files to `sources.cmake`, and new skill or other globbed files, before the first build of a worktree, and avoid committing between a cmake-file edit and the build that needs it. Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[pkill-cmake-build-leaves-ninja]].

Also learned that day: OrcaSlicer reinstalls its own `PlaterDropTarget` after every slice completes (`Plater::priv::on_process_completed`, `is_finished` is true for every non-slice-all run), so any fork-owned Plater drop target must be put back afterwards (the shell does it on idle).

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   Another Claude session (local_f472ffe1-987c-41db-a0a9-0bb20cb54657, "Upstream 2.5.0 rebase testing") started this session with this task. Kenneth agreed to the design elsewhere. JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer: `Updates::kVersion` = "2.0.0" in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp`, and `SoftFever_VERSION` = "2.5.0" must stay the number in project files. The task:
   1. **One shared fork header for OrcaSlicer's calls into JusPrin.** Make it `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/OrcaHooks.hpp`. GUI_App.cpp gets one JusPrin `#include` and one-line calls marked `// JusPrin:`. Move `JusPrin::apply_brand_palette()` (end of `GUI_App::init_label_colours`, ~line 4597) under that header, but keep it a separate call (it re-runs on every init_label_colours).
   2. **Startup hook** `JusPrin::startup_begin(*this)`, folded into OrcaSlicer's splash check in `GUI_App::on_init_inner` (~line 3451). It returns whether JusPrin showed its own splash, so OrcaSlicer skips its splash without writing `show_splash_screen`. Classic view is unchanged. The logic lives in fork-owned `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Startup/`, built so that a later startup stage costs one more upstream line.
   3. **JusPrin splash** with a moving indicator, not the 8-step percentage. JusPrin's existing shell attach code closes it, so there is no second upstream line. It shows `Updates::kVersion`.
   4. **JusPrin About window, with no upstream change.** AppMenus (fork-owned) finds both "&About JusPrin" items (Help on Windows/Linux, MainFrame.cpp ~2966; the macOS app menu, ~3615) and points them at the JusPrin window. The window shows:
      - the lockup
      - "Version 2.0.0" and "Built on OrcaSlicer 2.5.0"
      - the build commit and a Copy version button
      - jusprin-support@obico.io, Discord and GitHub https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin
      - a License button that opens OrcaSlicer's `CopyrightsDialog`

      Classic view keeps OrcaSlicer's About.
   5. **Design first** on the Claude canvas, with Kenneth's review, and every value from the design tokens.

   Done means all of the following:
   - The boards were reviewed.
   - The app is built on Kenneth's Mac with -j4.
   - It is checked in the real app with an isolated datadir: first launch, normal launch, classic view, the splash closing on time, and both About items opening the JusPrin window.
   - Windows and Linux compile through the GitHub "JusPrin nightly" workflow, run by hand.
   - The rebase evidence for each upstream line is written up.
   - The work is committed to this session's branch, with no push or merge without Kenneth's yes.

   Later instructions:
   - Kenneth chose "Yes, no bar there": the Windows and Linux splash has no moving bar, and the Mac has a Core Animation bar.
   - Kenneth said "boards are good. use Tx67dHNYH3 for discord invitation code", so Discord is https://discord.gg/Tx67dHNYH3.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Fork stewardship:** minimal upstream seams; additive edits; rebase evidence via `git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<last release taken> <newest upstream release> HEAD`; account for every upstream line deleted or rewritten; state what the fork owns.
   - **Design-system rules:**
     - Never type a color, font, radius or control size; add the token to `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json` first, with a guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp`.
     - Layout spacing may stay literal on the scale (4/8/12/16/20/24/32/40/48).
     - Native code reads `ShellTheme` (`palette(dark)`, `metrics()`, `font(role)`) and dresses stock controls via `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`.
     - Run the guards `brand_tokens_tests`, `shell_theme_tests` and `npm test` in AgentUI.
   - **The animation problem:**
     - The main thread is blocked for ~10 s during startup (load_presets ~5 s, MainFrame ~5 s), so timer animation freezes.
     - A Core Animation layer animation (CABasicAnimation) keeps moving while the main thread is blocked (tested with a throwaway app).
     - NSProgressIndicator didn't visibly spin.
     - Windows `wxActivityIndicator` is generic and timer-based; GTK's is main-loop driven.
   - **About menu binding:** OrcaSlicer's `append_menu_item` binds `menu->Bind(wxEVT_MENU, cb, id)`. A handler bound later on the same menu runs first, so not calling Skip blocks OrcaSlicer's handler. Unbinding on uninstall restores classic view.
   - **Splash class:** wxSplashScreen subclass pattern as OrcaSlicer does: a blank bitmap, a paint handler bound on `m_window`, `FilterEvent` overridden as a no-op, `wxSPLASH_CENTRE_ON_SCREEN`, and `wxBORDER_NONE | wxFRAME_NO_TASKBAR` plus `wxSTAY_ON_TOP` on Apple, with the Wayland titlebar workaround.
   - **Classic view check:** `app_config->get("jusprin_shell") == "0"`, used in `attach_shell` in ShellController.cpp.
   - **Build commit:** `Slic3r::GUI::build_commit_label` (BuildCommit.hpp, upstream) holds `GIT_COMMIT_HASH GIT_COMMIT_SUFFIX` (short hash, "-dirty" suffix).
   - **clang-tidy:** `misc-include-cleaner` checks missing includes only, so the umbrella header needs `// IWYU pragma: export`.
   - **Build rules for a fresh worktree:**
     - Add new source files to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake` before the first build (a cmake edit can force a full rebuild).
     - Apple `.mm` files go in an `if (APPLE)` list (upstream lists them in src/slic3r/CMakeLists.txt ~895).

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

### 9. Verify the risk claim instead of reasoning about it

**Rule.** Before asserting that a change is or is not rebase-risky, check it. Three checks, each one command: does git actually conflict there; has upstream already converged on the same change; is the change a move or a duplication.

**Mechanism.** A coherent story about fork risk is not a true one, and every one of these is cheaper to check than to argue about. Reasoning alone reliably produces confident, wrong claims — that a lost change is "silent" when git stops for it, that a move is a "duplication," that a cosmetic difference is gratuitous when upstream shares it.

**The test.** Did I run the simulation, or am I describing what I expect it to say?

**Violation.** A report that lists which files are rebase-sensitive and calls the change narrow, without having run the merge simulation that would have found two lossy resolutions waiting in it.

### 10. Take each upstream release by merging from the release we last took

**Rule.** Take a new upstream release with a merge whose base is the upstream release the fork last took. Never run a plain `git merge` of upstream, and never rewrite the fork's history to take a release.

**Mechanism.** The fork follows upstream's release branches, and each release branch splits off upstream's development line on its own. A plain merge picks the common ancestor itself, a development-line commit from before both release branches. Its conflict list is then everything that differs between the two release branches: vendor profiles, translations, CI files, none of it ours. Naming the last release we took as the base limits the merge to the fork's own changes. That gives the same conflicts a replay would hit, resolved once, with no commits rewritten, so branches in progress merge forward without a rebase. Measured on 2026-11-07, going from v2.4.2 to v2.5.0: 22 conflicted files either way, and a branch in progress merged into the trial result with no conflicts.

**How.** In a worktree on a new branch from `jusprin-dev`, the development branch:

```bash
git rev-parse <new release>^{commit} > "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)/MERGE_HEAD"
git merge-recursive <last release taken> -- HEAD <new release>
```

Resolve the conflicts, then `git commit`. A later patch release on the same release branch, such as 2.5.1 after 2.5.0, needs no override: a plain `git merge` finds the right base.

**The test.** Is the merge base the release we last took, and not a commit on upstream's development line?

**Violation.** `git merge upstream/main` or `git merge v2.5.0` with no base given. Each produces thousands of conflicts in files JusPrin never edited.

## Before you finish

A change that touches upstream-owned files is not done until this is recorded in the handback or pull request:

1. **The rebase simulation and its result.** Run it against the newest upstream release, with the release the fork last took as the base (rule 10), and name both endpoint commits — measurements are not reproducible otherwise.

   ```bash
   git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<last release taken> <newest upstream release> HEAD
   ```

   For each conflicted file, state whether the natural resolution is correct or lossy. A lossy one is a defect to fix now, not a note for later.

2. **An account of every upstream line deleted or rewritten.** Where the logic went, and why an additive form was not possible.

3. **A statement of what the fork now owns.** Policy, a neutral seam, or upstream behavior. The third needs an explicit justification.

An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It is not proof that a future rebase will merge, and never proof that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the focused contract tests, the full native build, the real multi-plate workflow, native gizmo input, and the stock-behavior regression checks.

description: "How to drive the real built JusPrin app for a screenshot-per-step UX walkthrough (2026-10-28): scratch copies, the empty local_machines loop with the fake printer, why background app_* tools fail on Orca dialogs, and where screenshots land."
  type: project

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].
description: "Seven traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control (2026-11-04): in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args, wx Wrap reuse."
  type: reference

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
  type: project

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.
description: "How to capture the fork's wx popup menus on macOS for a pixel comparison against Windows captures, and why Windows text renders ~9% larger than the tokens intend."
  type: project

To compare Windows screenshots against macOS, run the same
`shell_integration_harness` fixture on both and capture each popup by window id.

**Why:** `screencapture` and any ScreenCaptureKit path fail from the Bash tool
("could not create image from display") — the Screen Recording grant belongs to a
process I cannot reach. The computer-use `app_screenshot` tool is the only route,
and it accepts a **raw CGWindowID**, not just ids from `app_list_windows`. Popups
never appear in `app_list_windows`, so enumerate them yourself.

**How to apply:**
- Build a tiny Swift lister (`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionOnScreenOnly)`
  filtered by pid). The fork's `HeaderMenu` popups show up at `layer=101`; the main
  window is `layer=0`. Feed that id to `app_screenshot` for native-resolution pixels.
- Drive clicks with a Swift `CGEvent` helper at **global** coords
  (window origin + local). The app need not be frontmost.
- Only the **chip halves** respond to synthetic clicks. The header's overflow "…",
  the split-button chevron, and the Home back button do not — that is a limitation
  of the automation, **not** an application bug. Use the harness's own
  `--header-visual` / `--review-visual` modes for those screens instead.
- While a popup is open, the next click anywhere only dismisses it. Budget two
  clicks. Escape does not close them.
- Put the window on the **Acer H226HQL** (1920x1080, non-Retina): the harness's
  1200x800 window is then 1:1 with a Windows capture at 100% scaling, so popup
  sizes compare directly. On the built-in Retina display they would not.

**Windows text is ~9% LARGER than macOS, not smaller.** `Label::sysFont`
(`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/Label.cpp:19`) multiplies the point size by 4/5 off Apple
to offset Windows' 96 DPI against macOS' 72 — but 96/72 x 4/5 = 1.067, so it
under-corrects. Measured on the chip: glyph height 12 px Windows vs 11 px macOS.
Consequence: fixed-width popups ellipsize *more* on Windows. Do not assume the 4/5
factor makes Windows text smaller. Mono text goes the other way (Courier New is
narrower than Menlo), so the chip itself comes out 346 px on Windows vs 353 on Mac.

See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[windows-gui-test-vm-gcp]],
[[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].

description: "Drive the built JusPrin app headlessly (even with the screen locked) by posting CGEvents to its pid with a tiny Swift tool; keys work, mouse clicks do not, and the send dialog is reachable by keyboard."
  type: project

When the Mac screen is locked (`ioreg -n Root -d1 | grep CGSSessionScreenIsLocked`), the computer-use MCP request is auto-denied, `screencapture` fails, and System Events sees zero windows. Key events still reach the app: a 15-line Swift program calling `CGEvent(keyboardEventSource:virtualKey:keyDown:).postToPid(pid)` (compile with `swiftc`) made the app slice on Cmd+R (keycode 15) and open the send dialog on Cmd+Shift+G (keycode 5). Mouse events posted the same way did nothing, even with the window number set on the event.

Inside `PrintHostSendDialog` (Orca `MsgDialog`), focus starts in the filename field; Tab (48) moves to the "Upload" button, Right (124) to "Upload and Print", Space (49) presses it, because Orca's custom `Button` handles Space/Return and arrow navigation itself. Return alone triggers plain "Upload" (the affirmative id), not print.

`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` still lists the app's on-screen windows with bounds while locked, which tells you when a modal dialog is open (a small layer-0 window appears) and when it closed.

**Why:** On 2026-09-07 the end-to-end proof of the fake Moonraker printer needed the Print button pressed while the screen was locked; this was the only working path.

**How to apply:** Confirm the target pid first (`pgrep -f <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS`) so keys never go to another session's instance. Watch the app's own `--datadir` `log/debug_*.log` for effects (use `/usr/bin/grep -a`; the default `grep` is ugrep, which treats `\|` literally and may skip the log as binary). See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]].

   - **Fork stewardship rule 10 / "Before you finish":**
     - Run `git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<last release taken> <newest upstream release> HEAD`.

     - Account for each upstream line, and state what the fork owns.
   - **wx event order:** handlers bound later run first. MainFrame binds wxEVT_SHOW (MainFrame.cpp:828) after attach_shell (MainFrame.cpp:657) and doesn't Skip, so a JusPrin wxEVT_SHOW bound on the frame never runs. wxSplashScreen is an app-wide wxEventFilter (FilterEvent sees every event first), which is what the fix uses.
   - A pushed event handler can't be safely removed during its own dispatch, so that approach was rejected.
   - **wxTopLevelWindow::Destroy:** it deletes immediately if the main loop isn't running. So inside FilterEvent the splash calls Hide() and then CallAfter(Destroy).
   - **Core Animation:** a CABasicAnimation on position.x keeps running while the main thread is stopped. The painted content must be drawn (Refresh/Update) before the bar is added and `[CATransaction flush]` runs.

input.content:
JusPrin's own splash and About window, behind one fork header in GUI_App

With the JusPrin view on, startup now shows a JusPrin splash and both
"About JusPrin" menu items (Help on Windows and Linux, the app menu on
macOS) open a JusPrin About window. Classic view keeps OrcaSlicer's splash
and About unchanged.

Splash (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Startup/):
- The JusPrin logo and "Version 2.0.0" (Updates::kVersion), with no
  percentage or status line. On macOS a Core Animation bar sweeps back and
  forth; it keeps moving while startup blocks the main thread. Windows and
  Linux show the same splash without the bar, since nothing there can
  animate while the main thread is busy.
- It closes when the main window is first shown. It watches for that
  wxEVT_SHOW as an app-wide event filter, because MainFrame binds its own
  wxEVT_SHOW handler later and does not Skip it, so a handler bound on the
  frame never runs.
- It also respects OrcaSlicer's show_splash_screen preference.

About window (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/AboutWindow.*):
- The lockup, "Version 2.0.0", "Built on OrcaSlicer 2.5.0", the build
  commit, and Copy version, which copies
  "JusPrin 2.0.0 (OrcaSlicer 2.5.0), build <commit>".
- Get help: jusprin-support@obico.io, discord.gg/Tx67dHNYH3 and the GitHub
  repository.
- License… opens OrcaSlicer's licence and credits window. That window is
  always parented to the main window, so About takes the focus back when
  it closes.
- AppMenus rebinds the existing About items to it; no upstream file
  changes for this.

Every colour, size and font comes from design-tokens.json through
ShellTheme (new: component.splash, component.about, the small secondary
and link buttons, progress_height, code_font). The Lucide icon rasterizer
moved out of HeaderControls into Shell/LucideIcon so the About window can
use it.

OrcaSlicer-owned file: src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp, 2 lines.
- The include of JusPrin/Brand/BrandPalette.hpp becomes an include of
  JusPrin/OrcaHooks.hpp, the one header for OrcaSlicer's calls into
  JusPrin. It re-exports BrandPalette.hpp, so the existing
  apply_brand_palette() call is untouched.
- In GUI_App::on_init_inner the splash condition gains a leading
  "!JusPrin::startup_begin(*this) &&". OrcaSlicer's splash code is not
  deleted or moved; it runs as before whenever JusPrin did not show its
  own splash.
The fork owns policy only: when to show its splash instead of
OrcaSlicer's. MainFrame is not changed.

Rebase simulation (fork-stewardship "Before you finish"):
- git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=v2.5.0 v2.5.0 HEAD: clean.
  v2.5.0 is both the release last taken and the newest release.
- Against upstream/main d0ca537ebe (202 commits past v2.5.0): RESULT_MAIN.
  Upstream has no change near either GUI_App line.

Tested on macOS (Release, isolated --datadir): first launch and a normal
launch show the JusPrin splash, which closes about 40 ms before the main
window appears; classic view shows OrcaSlicer's splash and About; About
from the app menu matches the design board; Copy version, the link focus
ring, Tab order (Copy version, Email, Discord, GitHub, License…), License…
and Escape all work. brand_tokens_tests and shell_theme_tests pass.
Not checked by hand: Windows and Linux (compile only, via the nightly
build), Wayland, dark mode.
